description.value: A voxel-based morphometry study of frontotemporal dementia examining correlations between grey matter volume and semantic performance and neuropsychiatric disturbance, with an FTD-versus-control comparison.

spans.text: Using VBM, we found evidence consistent with the hypothesis that the left anterior temporal neocortex has a critical role in semantic processing and show that the severity of behaviour disturbance, as measured by the NPI composite score, principally correlated with the degree of atrophy of mesial, particularly right-sided, frontal lobe areas in a large group of patients with FTD.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison and correlational VBM study of FTD cases and age-matched controls.

spans.text: Correlational studies in neurodegenerative disorders raise an important methodological concern.

Cases with FTD were deliberately heterogeneous in terms of both disease severity and the degree to which they exhibited either behavioural or semantic (or often both) abnormalities in order to obtain a range of performance that would be appropriate for correlative analyses.

The aim being that identification of different distributions of significant anatomical correlation for each covariate when drawn from a single cohort would reduce the likelihood of false-positive correlation due to non-specific neurodegeneration.
The study had the approval of the Local Regional Ethics Committee.

value: The finding of such a discrete correlation between bilateral atrophy in the mesial frontal lobe and the NPI score may shed new light on the neural underpinning of behavioural changes in FTD.
